title: Git Bisect for Your Data
why_read: A clever, well-explained application of database branching to enable git-bisect-style debugging of data anomalies over time is a genuinely useful technique for engineers.
analysis: The article proposes using time-travel database branching, apparently via Neon's branch-from-a-timestamp feature, to binary-search through historical data states and find exactly when a data bug was introduced, mirroring how git bisect finds a bad commit. It gives concrete performance numbers, such as ~1.7 seconds per probe and about 13 probes to search a 24-hour window at one-minute precision, making the technique's feasibility clear. This is a practical, well-quantified debugging technique that many engineers dealing with data integrity issues would find directly applicable. It's a good example of turning a database feature into a systematic debugging workflow rather than ad hoc log scrolling.
